title: Generic algebra embedding for finite etale open covers
statement: Let $X$ be an integral scheme, $U\subseteq X$ an open subscheme, and $P\to U$ a finite etale morphism [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let $V\subseteq X$ be a nonempty affine open with $A=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_X)$ and $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-sc-function-field]. Put $f:P\to X$ for the composite and $B=\Gamma(f^{-1}V,\mathcal O_P)$ with its structural $A$-algebra structure. There exists a commutative finite etale $K$-algebra $D$ and an injective $A$-algebra homomorphism $B\to D$, where the $A$-algebra structure on $D$ is induced through $A\to K$. The open $U$, the cover, and the generic algebra may be empty or zero.

source.place: Tags 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field) and 081I (flat base change of scheme-theoretic images); application to the generic-point map

proof.text: Put A = Gamma(X,V) and K = Frac(A). Mathlib functionField_isFractionRing_of_isAffineOpen identifies the function field of X with K as an A-algebra. Compose Spec of this isomorphism with X.fromSpecFunctionField to construct a:Spec K -> X. It is dominant and quasi-compact; quasi-compactness follows because Spec K is a finite topological space.

Form Q = U times_X Spec K. The projection q:Q -> Spec K is an open immersion. Its source is reduced and has at most one point; its target is Jacobson. Hence Mathlib isFinite_iff_locallyOfFiniteType_of_jacobsonSpace makes q finite, including when Q is empty. Form T = P times_U Q, with r:T -> Spec K the composite of its projection to Q and q. Both factors are finite and etale. Therefore T is affine and D = Gamma(T,top), with its structural K-algebra map, is finite and formally etale. Apply finite_appTop, HasRingHomProperty.iff_of_isAffine, and the natural isomorphism between K and Gamma(Spec K,top).

Paste the two pullback squares to see that s:T -> P is the base change of a along the flat composite f:P -> U -> X. Dominance of a and reducedness of X give scheme-theoretic dominance of a. Mathlib IsSchemeTheoreticallyDominant.of_isPullback gives scheme-theoretic dominance of s, and quasi-compactness also survives base change. Thus s.app on f inverse V is injective by Scheme.Hom.app_injective.

Every point of Spec K maps under a to the generic point of X, which belongs to the nonempty open V. The pullback square therefore identifies the inverse image of f inverse V under s with top. Compose s.app with the section isomorphism for this equality to obtain an injective B -> D. The formula fromSpecStalk_app, naturality of Spec section maps and GammaSpecIso, and A-linearity of the fraction-field isomorphism identify a.appLE on V with A -> K -> Gamma(Spec K,top). The pasted square and appLE_comp_appLE then show B -> D commutes with A, making it the required algebra homomorphism.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_finiteEtale_open_generic_algebra {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
    (U : X.Opens) (P : U.toScheme.FiniteEtale) (V : X.Opens) [Nonempty V]
    (hV : IsAffineOpen V) :
    letI : Algebra Γ(X, V) Γ(P.obj.left, (P.obj.hom ≫ U.ι) ⁻¹ᵁ V) :=
      ((P.obj.hom ≫ U.ι).app V).hom.toAlgebra
    ∃ (D : Type u) (_ : CommRing D) (_ : Algebra (FractionRing Γ(X, V)) D),
      Module.Finite (FractionRing Γ(X, V)) D ∧
      Algebra.FormallyEtale (FractionRing Γ(X, V)) D ∧
      letI : Algebra Γ(X, V) D :=
        Algebra.compHom D (algebraMap Γ(X, V) (FractionRing Γ(X, V)))
      ∃ e : Γ(P.obj.left, (P.obj.hom ≫ U.ι) ⁻¹ᵁ V) →ₐ[Γ(X, V)] D,
        Function.Injective e
